entities.summary: Henri de Tonti was an Italian-born French military officer and explorer who assisted René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle during the French colonization of the Americas from 1678 to 1686. Tonti was one of the first explorers to navigate and sail the upper Great Lakes. He also sailed the Illinois and the Mississippi, to its mouth and thereupon claimed the length of the Mississippi for Louis XIV of France. He is credited with founding the settlement that would become Peoria, Illinois. Tonti established the first permanent European settlement in the lower Mississippi valley, known as Poste de Arkansea, making him "The Father of Arkansas".

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Tonti's expedition down the Mississippi River led to the establishment of Poste de Arkansea, the first permanent European settlement in the lower Mississippi valley, which would eventually become Arkansas. This claim gave Louis XIV control over a significant portion of North America.
